To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the AiP activates the superficial layers of PER/EC, whereas LA activates the deep layers, (ii) the AiP and subcortically activated PER/EC network show distinct spatiotemporally activation patterns, (iii) the inhibitory network is involved in the regulation of the activity transfer in the PER/ EC network, (iv) the inhibitory system has a higher threshold than the excitatory system, and (v) the AiP has a lower threshold
the extent of activity in PER/EC is determined by the inhibitory system and that the AiP and subcortically projecting LA activate overlapping regions, in a distinct spatio-temporal manner.
the AiP activates the PER/EC in a rostro-caudally direction whereas the LA activates only the PER.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the perirhinal and entorhimal cortex in the regulation of information transfer from the cortex to the hippocampus.
the role of the inhibitory network in regulating the transfer of cortical and subcortex input through the PER/ EC network.
the functional role of the PER and the EC in information transfer to and from the hippocampus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PER and EC are not only the main output areas of the AiP and lateral amygdala, respectively, but also the main input areas of these structures.
AiP stimulation evokes activity in the PER/LEC network, whereas LA stimulation evokes activity mainly in the deep layers PER/EC network.
PER/EC network is a highly complex system with a dynamic and plastic nature that actively regulates the information transfer through this network.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PER/EC system acts as a gatekeeper for information transfer between the (sub)cortex and the hippocampal system.
PER/EC network is not only involved in the processing of cortical input, but also in the processing of subcortical input, such as that from the LA.

PER/EC network is a dynamic system that can be activated by both cortical and sub-cortical inputs and that the inhibtion plays a role in the regulation of the activity transfer through the PER-EC network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the perirhinal-entorhinal network can be recruited by both cortical and sub-cortical input and that this network actively controls the (sub)cortex-hippocampus transfer of activity.
the PER and EC are differentially recruited by the AiP, LA and the hippocampus.
the PER and EC receive distinct inputs from the AiP and amygdala.
